decision: Do not add ARP IP↔MAC identity features to the V1 package and do not train a V2 ARP-identity model from this corpus. ARP Spoofing remains a documented detection limitation.

a5_stateless_fit_probe.finding: Within frozen 25-packet windows, sender-IP conflict features fire on only 7/6423 spoofing FIT windows (~0.11%). Benign has equal or higher arp_ratio than spoofing, so the gap is not explained by more ARP.

a6_stateful_fit_probe.finding: Whole-PCAP state finds only 1 spoofing sender IP with >1 SHA (conflict_obs_ratio≈4.9%; first dual claim ~5464 packets / ~109s later). Publisher benign and profiling (especially ActiveBroker) show higher retrospective multi-MAC rates (≈43% / ≈26%) than spoofing — multi-MAC history is not spoof-specific on FIT.

recommended_next: Keep V1 deployment statement unchanged regarding ARP spoofing. Future work should target other blind spots (e.g. MQTT malformed-data) or a different dataset/capture regime if IP↔MAC spoof evidence is required.
